# Herdr: coalesce the per-refresh `wl` spawns into one consolidated read

## Problem statement

A Herdr default-view refresh runs **five separate `wl` subprocesses per pane per tick**: the four mandatory `wl list` subsets plus the `wl next` browse feed (`packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts`). Per-spawn Node bootstrap now dominates the cost (~66 % of the remaining 0.70 CPU-s/spawn is the bare-node floor), so F10 capped the achievable reduction at ~65 % with five spawns and missed the 60 % target (47.6 % achieved). The remaining lever is **fewer spawns**: one consolidated read per refresh tick.

## Users

- **Herdr pane operator** (producer/agent running several Herdr panes on one worklog): wants a responsive worklist without each pane burning CPU on five `wl` boots per tick.
- **Herdr plugin maintainer**: wants one simple, cacheable read seam instead of five coordinated queries with an in-flight memo.
- **wl CLI maintainer**: wants the consolidated command to reuse the existing DB-query and read-cache machinery, not fork it.

### Example user stories

- As a Herdr pane operator, when 4–5 panes refresh every 30 s against one shared worklog, total CPU consumption should drop to **≤ 0.4× the pre-F4 baseline** so the host stays responsive.
- As a Herdr plugin maintainer, I want `fetcher.ts` to issue **one `wl` read per refresh tick** (one DB open, one cache entry), with the displayed items unchanged.
- As an agent relying on the worklist, I want the **mandatory guarantees** (critical items, blocked items and the review queue always shown) preserved by tests.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A single `wl` invocation returns every subset the worklist needs — critical, in_review review queue, in-progress roots, blocked roots and the browse feed — as a **dedicated `wl worklist --json` command** (preferred) or an equivalent `--worklist-bundle` mode, sharing **one DB open and one read-cache entry**.
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` issues that single read per default-view refresh tick; the mandatory-subset guarantees (critical always shown, blocked always shown, review queue always shown) are preserved by tests.
- Measured with `bench/herdr-refresh-cycle.ts` (F10): total CPU-seconds per 30 s cycle with 4 panes drops to **≤ 0.4× the pre-F4 baseline (≤ 63.8 CPU-s)**, ideally ~5× fewer spawns.
- Cache correctness unchanged: identical JSON for identical DB state, write invalidation still bumps the state counter, and worktree / `--worklog-dir` behaviour is unchanged.
- Herdr refresh output is unchanged for the same DB state (existing fetcher tests + the spawn-reduction simulation pass).
- **Testing/validation:** new tests cover the consolidated command's response shape, read-cache hit and write-invalidation, the fetcher's single-spawn path, mandatory-subset guarantees and output parity with the per-subset path.
- **Documentation:** all related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs-site entries (notably `docs/dev/herdr-event-driven-refresh.md`).
- **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- **Pure read:** the bundle must not write. `wl next`'s auto re-sort is a write byproduct; the bundle must use `--no-re-sort`-style selection (or reuse the selection logic without the write) so the result is deterministically cacheable.
- **Cache reuse:** register the new invocation with the existing read-cache (`src/read-cache-cli.ts`), keyed by `(worklog-dir, argv)` and fingerprinted by the monotonic state counter; a mid-action write must not cache an unrepresentative payload.
- **Fail-open fallback:** if the consolidated read is unavailable or fails (older `wl`, malformed payload), the fetcher falls back to today's per-subset spawn path with unchanged behaviour.
- **No output change:** the consolidated response must feed the same `extractItems` → `selectWorkItems` → `regroupWorkItems` pipeline so ordering, grouping and audit enrichment are identical.
- **Bounded payload:** the browse feed stays limited by the caller's count; subsets are returned with the same filters (`--root-only` where applicable) so payload growth is bounded and no item duplication is unbounded.
- `--worklog-dir` (module override and per-call) and managed-worktree resolution semantics are unchanged.
- TypeScript/Node stack; match existing style; no new runtime dependency unless unavoidable.

## Existing state

- **fetcher.ts** — `fetchMandatorySubsets()` spawns four `wl list` queries in parallel (critical, review queue, in-progress roots, blocked roots); `fetchNextItems()` spawns `wl next` and calls `fetchMandatorySubsets()`, giving five spawns per default-view refresh. An in-flight fetch memo deduplicates *identical* concurrent reads (which collapses the review-queue state query into the review subset), and `fetchChildrenForItems` / `fetchActionableCount` already read in-process from SQLite via one refresh-scoped connection.
- **Read cache** — `src/read-cache.ts` / `src/read-cache-cli.ts` serve `list`, `next`, `show`, `search` and `status` JSON from a shared on-disk cache keyed by `(worklog-dir, argv)`, fingerprinted by a monotonic per-worklog-dir write counter; writes bump the counter and drop entries. `src/cli.ts` performs the lookup before loading the heavy command graph.
- **CLI commands** — `src/commands/*.ts` register subcommands through `src/plugin-types.ts` / `src/command-registry.ts`; `next.ts` owns the auto re-sort and the selection semantics; `list.ts` owns the filtered list queries.
- **Measurement** — `bench/herdr-refresh-cycle.ts` (F10, 4 panes × 30 s × 5 s tick, sums per-process CPU from spawn records) and `bench/herdr-refresh-perf.ts` (spawn-count/latency per refresh).
- **F10 numbers** — pre-F4 baseline 159.44 CPU-s/cycle, after F4–F7 83.58 CPU-s/cycle (47.6 % reduction), target 63.78; per-spawn 1.329 → 0.697 CPU-s against a ~0.46 CPU-s bare-node floor.

## Desired change

1. Add a consolidated worklist read to the `wl` CLI — preferably a new `wl worklist --json` command — that opens the database **once** and returns the critical, review-queue, in-progress-root, blocked-root and browse-feed subsets in one payload, built from the same query/selection code the individual commands use.
2. Make it a cacheable read invocation (one cache entry, same state-counter fingerprint and write invalidation), so repeat refreshes across panes hit the cache as a single entry.
3. Change `fetcher.ts` so the default-view refresh drives that one read (with the review-queue state and browse feed derived from it) and retains the existing per-subset path as a fail-open fallback.
4. Add coverage: command unit/integration tests, cache hit/invalidation tests, fetcher single-spawn and mandatory-guarantee tests, and an output-parity test against the per-subset path; update the spawn-reduction simulation and the benchmark expectations.
5. Update `docs/dev/herdr-event-driven-refresh.md` and any CLI reference docs/comments.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/commands/worklist.ts` — **new** consolidated read command (or a `--worklist-bundle` mode added to `src/commands/list.ts`)
- `src/command-registry.ts` — register the new command
- `src/read-cache-cli.ts` — add the invocation to `READ_CACHE_COMMANDS` / cacheability checks
- `src/cli.ts` — cache lookup path (expected unchanged; verify the new command is served before the heavy graph)
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — single consolidated read, review-state/browse derivation, fail-open fallback
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — `doRefresh` wiring so the bundle replaces the per-subset fan-out
- `tests/cli/read-cache-spawn-reduction.test.ts` — spawn-reduction simulation uses the consolidated invocation
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher-*.test.ts` — mandatory-subset, review-queue and output-parity coverage
- `bench/herdr-refresh-cycle.ts` — measurement harness (expects the consolidated query)
- `docs/dev/herdr-event-driven-refresh.md` — cold-refresh cost section updated

## Related work

- **F10 — WL-0MVFRRS2I000G93J** (completed): measured the <= 60 % shortfall and filed this item with the spawn-count lever. This item is the follow-up implementation of that lever.
- **WL-0MVFNMSRW002FI6B** (completed, outbound dependency): spawn-load epic — transient `wl` process CPU usage.
- **WL-0MV5CBQ6L005SPAG** (completed): cut cold refresh cost — in-process SQLite reads, in-flight fetch memo, batched expanded children. The consolidated read builds on this.
- **WL-0MV6C6SLB005HX7B** (completed): one shared in-process connection per refresh — related "one open per refresh" precedent.
- **WL-0MV02VA29009WBEN** (completed): make Herdr refresh snappy after agent updates — parent of the earlier performance work.
- **Docs:** `docs/dev/herdr-event-driven-refresh.md`, `docs/dev/wl-spawn-baseline-2026-10-19.md`, `docs/benchmarks/wal-read-latency-benchmark.md`.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Cache staleness (risk, high):** a single cache entry must never serve stale data across a write. Mitigation: reuse the counter fingerprint, cache only when the counter is unchanged since lookup, and add an explicit write-invalidation test.
- **Re-sort write byproduct (risk, medium):** today's `wl next` runs an auto re-sort (a DB write) on some invocations. The bundle must be a pure read; assumption: `--no-re-sort` selection produces the same displayed order for a stable DB. Verify with an output-parity test; if ordering genuinely differs, resolve the re-sort as a separate, explicitly-documented concern rather than making the bundle a write.
- **Mandatory-subset regression (risk, high):** a bundle that silently drops a subset breaks the always-shown guarantees. Mitigation: tests assert each mandatory subset is present regardless of the browse window.
- **Backwards compatibility (risk, low):** an older `wl` without the new command. Mitigation: fall back to the per-subset spawn path (fail-open).
- **Cross-subset consistency (risk, medium):** the five subsets are read in one process but through separate queries; a write landing mid-bundle could make the subsets disagree. Mitigation: serve all subsets from one DB connection inside a read transaction (or the same store snapshot) so the payload reflects one stable state; at minimum, match today's eventual-consistency behaviour and document it.
- **Payload size (risk, low):** five subsets in one payload. Mitigation: keep the browse feed count-bounded and reuse the existing dedupe/merge pipeline.
- **Scope creep (risk, medium):** further per-spawn startup optimisation (F4–F7) is out of scope. Record additional opportunities as linked work items, not scope.
- **Assumption:** `wl` and the Herdr plugin ship together from this repository, so the fetcher may rely on the new command in the same release; the fallback remains for robustness.

## Verification plan

```sh
# CPU-seconds per 30 s cycle, 4 panes (F10 harness)
npm run benchmark:herdr-refresh -- --json --items 20 --cycle-seconds 30 --tick-seconds 5

# Spawn count and latency for a single default-view refresh
npx tsx bench/herdr-refresh-perf.ts --json
```

- Compare the measured CPU-seconds against the ≤ 63.8 CPU-s target and the pre-F4 baseline quoted above.
- Run the changed-scope and full test suites via `/skill:test`.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q:** Was an interview needed for this intake?
  **A (agent, based on repo evidence):** No. The seed context already contains a measured problem, a quantified target, explicit acceptance criteria and a named lever, so the brief was drafted directly from that plus a repo inspection. Source: work item description and F10 comment.
- **Q:** Which command shape should the consolidated read take?

# Remove dead top-level `singleFork` key in vitest.config.ts

**discovered-from:** WL-0MVF9JJUH0077OB8 — Reduce time to run tests

## Problem statement

`vitest.config.ts` sets `singleFork: true` at the top level of the `test`
block. Vitest 4 has no such top-level option — `singleFork` is a
`poolOptions.forks.*` key — so the setting is silently ignored (no warning is
emitted). The comment directly above it, "Force per-file isolation by limiting
to 1 active worker per file sequence", describes behaviour that is actually
provided by `isolate: true` + `maxWorkers: 4` (+ `pool: 'forks'`).

The dead key is harmless today, but it is misleading: a future reader may
believe the suite is serialised, and a migration to an option shape that *is*
read (or vitest version churn that starts warning) could confuse diagnosis.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `singleFork: true` is removed from `vitest.config.ts`.
- The comment above it is rewritten (or removed) to state what actually
  enforces per-file isolation (`pool: 'forks'`, `isolate: true`,
  `maxWorkers: 4`), and that parallelism is otherwise intentional.
- Full canonical suite (`tests/cli` + `tests/unit`) stays green with the same
  test counts; no runtime regression in either wall-clock or aggregate test
  time on the same host.

## Out of scope

Bumping `maxWorkers` / `fileParallelism` — that is the follow-up "Test-suite
parallelism: reconsider maxWorkers on hosts with more cores".

# Investigate in-process CLI harness cost (~200 ms per invocation)

**discovered-from:** WL-0MVF9JJUH0077OB8 — Reduce time to run tests

## Problem statement

Timing the in-process CLI harness (`tests/cli/cli-inproc.ts`,
`runInProcess()`, used by `execAsync` in `tests/cli/cli-helpers.ts`):

- `--help` (no DB work): ~72 ms per invocation
- `list --json`, `create`, `status`: ~196–257 ms per invocation

The canonical suite (`tests/cli` + `tests/unit`) makes roughly 1200 such
in-process invocations — about 240 s of aggregate test time across
`close-recursive` (46 tests), `issue-management` (49), `issue-status` (43),
`valid-json-output` (38) and `json-output-shape` (18), plus seeding in
`beforeEach` hooks.

Every invocation constructs a fresh `Command`, re-registers ~35 built-in
commands, loads config, opens a SQLite database (with schema/migrations) and
closes it. The suite measured 624 s → 427–547 s after WL-0MVF9JJUH0077OB8, and
this in-process pool is the next largest remaining aggregate.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Profile one `runInProcess` call and attribute the per-call cost
  (commander registration vs config load vs DB open/close vs command action).
- Where the cost is test-harness overhead (not production behaviour being
  asserted), reduce it without changing what each test asserts — candidates:
  reusing the command/plugin-context across calls for stateless reads,
  avoiding repeated YAML config parses, sharing DB open across calls within a
  test file.
- If the cost is production CLI startup (DB schema/migrations, plugin scan),
  record the findings and re-scope: the change then belongs in `src/` and is a
  production decision, not a test-only change.
- Canonical suite stays green with unchanged test counts; median wall-clock
  on a consistent host improves versus the pre-change baseline of this item.

**discovered-from:** WL-0MVF9JJUH0077OB8 — Reduce time to run tests

## Problem statement

The canonical suite (`tests/cli` + `tests/unit`) runs with `maxWorkers: 4`
in `vitest.config.ts` (pool `'forks'`, `isolate: true`). The dev host has 16
cores. WL-0MVF9JJUH0077OB8 reduced per-spawn cost ~5× (bundle-based CLI
spawning) and cut the wall clock 30–35 % at matched load, but wall clock
remains dominated by the longest single files on the critical path
(`sync-vs-mutation` ~151 s, `close-recursive` ~121 s, `issue-management`
~88 s, `read-cache-spawn-reduction` ~84 s).

The brief explicitly listed parallelisation as out of scope ("record as
linked follow-up work items, not this brief") — hence this item.

- Measure the canonical suite at `maxWorkers` 4 vs 6 vs 8 on a 16-core host
  (median of ≥3 runs per setting, load quoted per run; report aggregate test
  time as the load-independent metric).
- Confirm memory headroom: RSS per worker tracked; no OOM at the chosen
  setting (the config comment cites memory guardrails as the reason for 4).
- Confirm determinism: 3 consecutive green runs at the chosen setting, no
  intermittent test-timeout or hook-timeout failures.
- Decide and record: either adopt a higher `maxWorkers` (documented) or
  formally keep 4 with the measurement evidence.

# Maintenance routines skill: create/maintain daily scheduled test, standup, refactor sessions at high priority

## Headline

A new ContextHub skill (`/skill:maintenance-routines`) that creates and maintains the required daily scheduled maintenance sessions (test 07:00, standup 08:00, refactor 09:00) in each project's `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json`, dispatching all of them at **high request priority** so they are processed even in peak periods — backed by a herdr enhancement that threads a per-entry `priority` (default `high`) into the `X-Priority` request header.

## Problem statement

Every project should run regular automated maintenance routines (test suite, standup report, refactor pass). The herdr plugin already has the mechanism (`scheduled-prompts.json`, dispatched on idle by the downtime worker), but there is no maintained, canonical set: the current template/live config only carries `/skill:refactor` (3-day interval, no time) and `/skill:standup` (06:05, no priority), and **no** `/skill:test` routine. Worse, dispatched scheduled prompts have no work item, so they receive the downtime request-priority default `medium` (`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` `buildDowntimeSpawnOptions` → `mapDowntimeRequestPriority(undefined)` → `medium`) — they can be starved behind peak-period contention. The operator wants the three routines scheduled daily (07:00/08:00/09:00) and dispatched at **high** priority.

## Users

- **Project operator** — wants the three routines to reliably exist in each project's schedule and to be processed even in peak periods.
- **Automated maintenance sessions** (`/skill:test`, `/skill:standup`, `/skill:refactor`) — must carry `X-Priority: high` on every provider request so `llama-proxy` serves them ahead of the contention queue.

### Example user stories

- As an operator, I run `/skill:maintenance-routines` on a project and it ensures `/skill:test` (daily 07:00), `/skill:standup` (daily 08:00) and `/skill:refactor` (daily 09:00) are present and correctly configured in `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json`, without touching my last-run timestamps or any custom entries.
- As an operator, I know every scheduled maintenance session is dispatched with `HERDR_REQUEST_PRIORITY=high` (→ `X-Priority: high`), so the daily test/standup/refactor runs are served even during peak periods.
- As an operator, when I provision a new project with `wl init`, it comes pre-loaded with the same three routines (daily, timed, high priority).

## Acceptance criteria

1. **Skill exists and reconciles the schedule.** `skill/maintenance-routines/` ships a `SKILL.md`, a reconciler script and unit tests. Invoking it (or the script directly) reconciles the project-local `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json` (under the resolved worklog dir) so these required routines are present and exact:
   - `/skill:test` — `intervalDays: 1`, `time: "07:00"`, `priority: "high"`
   - `/skill:standup` — `intervalDays: 1`, `time: "08:00"`, `priority: "high"`
   - `/skill:refactor` — `intervalDays: 1`, `time: "09:00"`, `priority: "high"`
2. **Reconcile is non-destructive and idempotent.** Entries are created if absent; drifted fields (interval/time/priority) are corrected; `lastTriggeredAt` and all other user-defined entries are preserved verbatim; a second run makes no further changes; missing or malformed config files are handled fail-closed with a clear report; `--dry-run` shows the planned diff without writing.
3. **Herdr honours a per-entry `priority` field.** `ScheduledPrompt` gains an optional `priority` (`low|medium|high|critical`) validated in `parseScheduledPrompt` (invalid value → entry skipped with a warning, fail-closed); **absent → defaults to `high`** for scheduled prompts. The scheduled-prompt dispatch passes it through `spawnAgentPane({ priority })` → `buildDowntimeSpawnOptions` → `HERDR_REQUEST_PRIORITY` (so `high` → `X-Priority: high` on every request). Unit tests cover parse defaults/validation and the dispatch threading.
4. **Template provisions the required set.** `templates/scheduled-prompts.json` (the `wl init` base set) is updated to the three required routines with daily `intervalDays`, `time` and `priority: high`, so new projects are provisioned with the routines (create-if-absent semantics unchanged — existing configs are never clobbered).
5. **Documentation criterion.** `packages/herdr/README.md` (Scheduled prompts section), `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` (Request priority section) and `CONFIG.md` (Scheduled-prompts config section) document the new `priority` field, the default-`high` behaviour, and the three routines; the maintenance-routines skill is referenced from the relevant skill docs listing.
6. **Testing criterion.** Skill tests (`pytest` under `skill/maintenance-routines/tests/`) cover reconcile/idempotence/preservation/dry-run; herdr unit tests (`vitest`) cover the new parse/validation and dispatch priority; full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **No changes to the interactive dispatch path or to the other downtime tiers' mapping tables** (`request-priority.ts` stays fixed); only the scheduled-prompt entry schema, its dispatch call, and the skill/template change.
- The requested **default is `high`** for scheduled prompts (operator decision Q1): an entry that wants lower priority must set the field explicitly (`low`/`medium`). This is a deliberate change from the current downtime default (`medium`) for scheduled prompts only.
- No code-behaviour changes to `wl init` — only the **contents** of `templates/scheduled-prompts.json` (the provisioning path and create-if-absent semantics stay as-is).
- The skill must be safe to run from any project root (`wl`-independent — it reads/writes only `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json`, atomic tmp+rename, matching herdr's `saveScheduledPrompts` pattern).

## Existing state

- `templates/scheduled-prompts.json` (and the live `/.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json`) currently carry only `/skill:refactor` (3-day interval, no time) and `/skill:standup` (daily `time: "06:05"`); no `/skill:test`; no priority field anywhere.
- `packages/herdr/src/scheduled-prompts.ts` — schema (`id|prompt|intervalDays|lastTriggeredAt|time?`), fail-closed parse, due-check, atomic persist; **no priority support**.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — `dispatchScheduledPrompt` calls `spawnAgentPane(prompt.prompt, { model, cwd, paneName, anchorId })` with **no priority** → `buildDowntimeSpawnOptions({ priority: undefined })` → `mapDowntimeRequestPriority(undefined)` → `medium` (docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md, "Scheduled prompts have no work item and get the downtime default (medium)").
- `src/commands/init.ts` — `ensureScheduledPromptsInstalled` copies the template create-if-absent; unchanged in behaviour.
- Skills precedent: `skill/heartbeat/` and `skill/pane-triage/` (SKILL.md + scripts + tests, tracked in ContextHub, deployed to `~/.pi/agent/skills/<name>`); shared helpers in `skill/shared/`.

## Desired change

1. **New skill** `skill/maintenance-routines/`: `SKILL.md` (spec: required-routines table, invocation, admission of a bootstrap `/skill:maintenance-routines` schedule), `scripts/maintenance_routines.py` (reconcile + `--dry-run`; atomic writes; preserves `lastTriggeredAt` and foreign entries), `tests/` (unit tests).
2. **Herdr priority support**: extend `ScheduledPrompt` + `parseScheduledPrompt` with optional `priority` (default `high`); thread it from `dispatchScheduledPrompt` → `spawnAgentPane({ priority })` → `buildDowntimeSpawnOptions` → `HERDR_REQUEST_PRIORITY`. `mapDowntimeRequestPriority` already maps `high`→`high`.
3. **Template**: update `templates/scheduled-prompts.json` to the three routines (daily, timed, `priority: "high"`).
4. **Docs**: `packages/herdr/README.md`, `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`, `CONFIG.md`; skill listed alongside heartbeat/pane-triage where appropriate.
5. **Tests**: pytest for the skill reconciler; vitest for parse/validation + dispatch threading in herdr.

## Key Files

- `skill/maintenance-routines/SKILL.md` — new skill spec (required-routines table, usage, dry-run).
- `skill/maintenance-routines/scripts/maintenance_routines.py` — new reconciler CLI (`--dry-run`, atomic write, preserves state).
- `skill/maintenance-routines/tests/test_maintenance_routines.py` — new unit tests (reconcile, idempotence, preservation, malformed config, dry-run).
- `packages/herdr/src/scheduled-prompts.ts` — add optional `priority` (`low|medium|high|critical`, default `high`), validation in `parseScheduledPrompt`.
- `packages/herdr/src/scheduled-prompts.test.ts` — new parse/default/validation cases.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — `dispatchScheduledPrompt` passes `prompt.priority` to `spawnAgentPane`.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts` (or the scheduled-prompts tier test) — dispatch threads `priority: 'high'` into the spawn opts/env.
- `templates/scheduled-prompts.json` — updated to the three required routines.
- `packages/herdr/README.md`, `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`, `CONFIG.md` — document the new field/default and the routines.
- `tests/skill/maintenance-routines/` — integration-style tests for the skill (repo test-suite convention, cf. `tests/skill/heartbeat/`).

## Related work

- **WL-0MSS1Q5ER007QDKX** (completed) — herdr downtime dispatcher: scheduled prompts (best-effort frequency) config — the mechanism the skill maintains.
- **WL-0MVE1NZ4J000H5NH / WL-0MVF3Q3VL000UNCN** (completed) — request priority (`X-Priority`) mapping tables and `HERDR_REQUEST_PRIORITY` env threading — the priority plumbing we reuse.
- **WL-0MTF5UAJ4000LLZ9** (completed) — removal of scheduled-prompts console output (no-op here).
- **WL-0MUKYERLZ006ELL5** (completed) — non-terminal cooldown for dispatched panes (context for scheduled dispatch behaviour).
- **WL-0MRHYQU1S009DJ9B** (completed) — periodic request scheduling to the pi worklog plugin; the scheduled-prompts feature parent.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MRHYQU1S009DJ9B** – Add periodic request scheduling to pi worklog plugin (completed)
- **WL-0MTMN7W63001FCQR** – Scheduled prompts: add time-of-day dispatch (time window) to scheduled-prompts tier (completed)
- **WL-0MKRPG64S04PL1A6** – wl doctor (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: convey, create, creates, currently, daily (+26 more)
- `CHANGELOG.md` — matched: create, creates, daily, default, dispatched (+25 more)
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — matched: convey, create, creates, currently, default (+23 more)
- Skill-authoring precedents: `skill/heartbeat/`, `skill/pane-triage/` (SKILL.md + scripts + tests, deployed to `~/.pi/agent/skills`).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — default-`high` changes politeness of ALL scheduled prompts** (including custom future entries). Accepted by operator (Q1: "default high"); any entry can opt down via an explicit `low`/`medium` field. Mitigation: document prominently.
- **Risk — parse strictness.** An invalid `priority` value rejects the whole entry (consistent with existing `time` handling) — a config typo could silently disable a routine. Mitigation: the skill always writes a valid value; tests cover the failure path.
- **Risk — skill/template drift.** If `templates/scheduled-prompts.json` is later edited, the skill's required table may diverge. Mitigation: keep the required-routines table in one place (the skill), and the template mirrors it (as Q3).
- **Assumption — the skill runs per project root.** Invoked via a pi session (herdr pane or manual) with `cwd` at the project root; it reads/writes only `<cwd>/.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json` (worklog-dir safe).
- **Assumption — operators may bootstrap the skill itself as a scheduled prompt** (e.g. daily `/skill:maintenance-routines`) to keep the schedule self-healing; not required for this item.
- **Scope-creep guard:** no changes to interactive dispatch, `request-priority.ts` tables, other downtime tiers, or `wl init` code; any opportunity discovered during implementation is recorded as a new linked work item, not added here.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1: How should scheduled routines get high priority?**
  - Options: (a) per-entry `priority` field in `scheduled-prompts.json`, threaded through herdr dispatch → `HERDR_REQUEST_PRIORITY`; (b) herdr always dispatches all scheduled prompts at `high`; (c) config-level default priority.
  - **Answer (producer, interactive reply): "1. A (default high)"** — per-entry field; **absent → default `high`**.
  - Reasoning recorded: matches "all those work items should be sent high priority so they get processed even in peak periods"; keeps intent in the config; future entries can opt down explicitly.
- **Q2: How strictly should the skill maintain the required set?**
  - Options: (a) ensure the three required routines exist & match spec (create-if-absent, fix drifted fields), keep other user entries; (b) strict whitelist (remove anything else); (c) create-if-absent only (never fix drift).
  - **Answer (producer): "2. A"** — non-destructive reconcile, preserve custom entries.
- **Q3: Should new projects get the routines by default?**
  - Options: (a) also update `templates/scheduled-prompts.json` (the `wl init` base set); (b) skill-only.
  - **Answer (producer): "3. A"** — template updated so every new project provisions the three routines at 07:00/08:00/09:00 high (`wl init` code path unchanged).

## Failure Signature

- Test file: `tests/cli/completion.test.ts`
- Failing cases (2 — one per shell):
  - `wl completion bash > contains all known subcommands`
  - `wl completion zsh > contains all known subcommands`
- Failure: `AssertionError: expected completion script to contain "worklist"` — the generated script's command list omits `worklist` (`audit … unlock update completion`, no `worklist`).
- Failing commit: surfaced on `dev` after `c8d8197f` (WL-0MVI0HX58009JJRF, 2026-10-21 19:28).
- CI job: (not available)

## Root Cause (verified during planning)

**The source is correct; the failure is a stale-build artefact.** Two facts
combine:

1. **`tests/cli/completion.test.ts` spawns the *built* CLI and bypasses the
   build-freshness guard.** It hard-codes its entry point:

   ```ts
   const CLI_PATH = resolve(__dirname, '../../dist/cli.js');
   ```

   `dist/` is gitignored (`.gitignore:86`) and `npm test` does not rebuild it,
   so this file asserts against whatever build happens to be on disk — not
   against `src/`.

2. **The checked-out `dist/` predated the `worklist` command.** Observed
   state: `dist/cli.js` mtime `2026-10-21 15:52:42`; commits
   `c8d8197f` (19:28:20, adds `src/commands/worklist.ts` +
   `worklist` in `BUILT_IN_COMMAND_NAMES`) and `e1cedba5` (20:12:33) landed
   afterwards. `grep -c worklist dist/cli.js` → `0`; `dist/commands/worklist.js`
   did not exist.

**Verification performed (reproduce → rebuild → pass):**

```bash
node dist/cli.js completion bash | grep -c worklist   # 0  (stale build)
npm run build
node dist/cli.js completion bash | grep -c worklist   # 2  (command + id-arg list)
node dist/cli.js completion zsh  | grep -c worklist   # 1
```

`worklist` is the **only** required command missing from the stale script
(`init status create list show update delete export import next in-progress
sync github comment close recent plugins migrate dep re-sort doctor search
unlock audit completion` all appear), which is exactly why the single
assertion that tripped names `worklist`.

**Why this is not simply "rebuild and move on":** a rebuild fixes this
checkout but commits nothing (`dist/` is gitignored), so the same false
failure returns for any checkout whose build lags `src/`. The repo already
solved this class of problem twice:

- WL-0MVF9JJUH0077OB8 converted every `dist/cli.js`-spawning test to the
  pre-compiled bundle helper `tests/cli/cli-bundle.ts` ("as a side effect now
  run against current `src/` instead of whatever build happened to be on
  disk") and added the regression guard `tests/unit/no-tsx-cli-spawn.test.ts`
  — see `docs/dev/test-suite-baseline.md`
  § "Change (test code + test config only)". **`completion.test.ts` was missed
  by that sweep.**
- WL-0MVH44JRR000A23U (same failure class, `entry-point-split.test.ts`) fixed
  `isDistFresh()` so `resolveStartupTarget('auto', …)` never selects a stale
  build.

So the durable fix is to finish the missed sweep for this file and make the
regression guard cover the *hard-coded `dist/` spawn* idiom, not only the
`tsx` idiom.

## Steps To Reproduce

1. From a checkout whose `dist/cli.js` predates the `worklist` command
   (`stat -c '%y' dist/cli.js` older than `git log -1 -- src/commands/worklist.ts`):
   - `npx vitest run tests/cli/completion.test.ts -t 'contains all known subcommands'`
2. Observe `expected completion script to contain "worklist"` for both the
   bash and zsh cases.
3. `npm run build` and re-run — both pass. (Confirmed during planning.)

## Desired Change

Keep it to test code, one new regression guard, and docs. No production code
change: `src/commands/completion.ts` already emits `worklist` correctly once
built from `HEAD`.

1. **Fix `tests/cli/completion.test.ts`** — resolve its CLI under test through
   the established, always-in-sync helper instead of `dist/cli.js`:
   `runCliProcess(['completion', 'bash'])` from `tests/cli/cli-bundle.ts`
   (esbuild bundle of `src/cli.ts`, built once per test process, tsx fallback
   when esbuild is unavailable). Keep the existing assertions and the
   `--json`/unknown-shell/usage cases intact; only the spawn path changes.
2. **Extend the regression guard** — add `tests/unit/no-stale-dist-spawn.test.ts`
   (modelled on `tests/unit/no-tsx-cli-spawn.test.ts`): scan `tests/**/*.ts`
   for the `dist/cli.js` spawn idiom and fail for any file outside a
   documented allowlist, with a message pointing at
   `runCliProcess()`/`cliInvocation()`.
   - Allowlist rationale (each entry needs a one-line reason in the test):
     `tests/cli/entry-point-split.test.ts` and
     `tests/cli/startup-import-budget.test.ts` intentionally exercise the built
     entry (both go through the freshness-aware `resolveStartupTarget` /
     explicit-dist contract), `tests/unit/startup-target-freshness.test.ts`
     uses temp fixtures, `tests/unit/no-stale-dist-spawn.test.ts` is the scanner
     itself, and `tests/cli/smoke.test.ts` asserts that the *built* artefact
     loads — that is its purpose.
3. **Migrate the remaining hard-coded spawn** —
   `tests/cli/doctor-foreign-items-push.test.ts` (`cliPath =
   path.join(projectRoot, 'dist', 'cli.js')`) should use `cliInvocation()`.
   If it proves load-bearing in a surprising way, allowlist it with a reason
   rather than blocking the guard.
4. **Docs** — update `docs/dev/test-suite-baseline.md` (§ the cli-bundle sweep)
   to record that `completion.test.ts` (+ `doctor-foreign-items-push.test.ts`)
   now use the bundle, that `no-stale-dist-spawn.test.ts` is the second guard,
   and to restate the standing rule: **tests must not hard-code `dist/cli.js`;
   `npm run build` is required before a bare checkout's suite, and the guard
   keeps that from silently producing false failures.**

## Implementation Notes (for implement phase)

- **Red-first evidence cannot come from the ambient checkout.** `implement.py`
  runs `npm run build` before tests, so in a worktree both shells already pass.
  Drive the guard test red by fixture: create a temp `tests/`-like tree (or
  pass a root parameter) containing a file that spawns `dist/cli.js` and assert
  the scanner reports it — mirror `startup-target-freshness.test.ts` (temp dirs
  + controlled content) rather than mutating real mtimes.
- **Alternative considered and rejected:** switch to
  `resolveStartupTarget('auto', repoRoot)` + `buildStartupInvocation(...)`.
  Correct, but slower than the bundle and leaves this file on the tsx fallback
  path when `dist/` is stale; the bundle is the repo's stated convention for
  "a real subprocess is needed".
- Completion output includes plugin-provided commands (e.g. `stats`) — plugin
  loading is independent of the entry point, so the bundle produces the same
  command list as `dist/cli.js`.
- Do **not** touch `src/commands/completion.ts`, `bench/wl-startup-perf.ts` or
  `tests/cli/cli-bundle.ts` — all three are already correct.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `npx vitest run tests/cli/completion.test.ts` passes against the latest
  `dev` **both with a fresh `dist/` and with a deliberately stale/absent
  `dist/`** (the file no longer depends on ambient build state).
- [ ] `tests/cli/completion.test.ts` no longer hard-codes `dist/cli.js`; it
  spawns the CLI through `tests/cli/cli-bundle.ts`
  (`runCliProcess`) and keeps every existing assertion (bash script shape,
  known subcommands, global options, dynamic work-item ID completion,
  completion-of-completion, unknown-shell error, `--json` payload) intact.
- [ ] A new guard test `tests/unit/no-stale-dist-spawn.test.ts` fails when any
  test file outside a documented allowlist spawns a hard-coded `dist/cli.js`,
  and its failure message names the offending file and the recommended helper
  (red-first: proven against a fixture input, not only against the current
  tree).
- [ ] `tests/cli/doctor-foreign-items-push.test.ts` either uses
  `cliInvocation()` or is allowlisted with a written reason.
- [ ] The two originally failing cases (`wl completion bash|zsh > contains all
  known subcommands`) pass, with `worklist` present in both generated scripts.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes
  (`docs/dev/test-suite-baseline.md`: cli-bundle sweep completeness, the new
  stale-dist guard, and the standing "tests must not hard-code `dist/`" rule).
- [ ] Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Key Files

- `tests/cli/completion.test.ts` — spawn the CLI via `runCliProcess()`; drop `CLI_PATH`.
- `tests/unit/no-stale-dist-spawn.test.ts` — new repo-wide guard (modelled on `no-tsx-cli-spawn.test.ts`).
- `tests/cli/doctor-foreign-items-push.test.ts` — remaining hard-coded `dist/cli.js` spawn; migrate or allowlist.
- `tests/cli/cli-bundle.ts` — reused (`runCliProcess`/`cliInvocation`); no change expected.
- `tests/unit/no-tsx-cli-spawn.test.ts` — the guard pattern to mirror (read-only reference).
- `tests/unit/startup-target-freshness.test.ts` — fixture-with-temp-dirs pattern for the guard's red-first evidence (read-only reference).
- `docs/dev/test-suite-baseline.md` — documentation update (sweep completeness + guard + standing rule).
- `src/commands/completion.ts` — verified correct; **no change expected**.

## Related work

- `WL-0MVI0HX58009JJRF` — added the `worklist` command and the
  `worklist` entry in `KNOWN_COMMANDS` (commit `c8d8197f`); its suite run had a
